deviations.D1_hardware: The GPU is an NVIDIA L4 (23 GB, Ada, sm_89), not the planned RTX A4500 (Ampere, 20 GB); exp23 ran on an RTX 2000 Ada. Gemma runs in bf16 as planned. The engine check reproduces exp23's labels on 100% of matched slots (T1 twin, T1 esc9003 alpha 1, T2 twin), so the engine difference is immaterial at the label level; every contrast is computed within this artifact's engine anyway.
deviations.D2_U3_tolerance: GPU test U3: the realised push component along u matches alpha x n within 0.18% (max over rows and band blocks), not the plan's 0.1%. The residual is bf16 rounding of the edited state at Gemma's massive-activation scale (|h| ~ 17,700 at spec positions; bf16 spacing 16-64 in the massive channels) and is far inside exp23's 1% tolerance; U1, U2, U4 and U9 pass exactly.
deviations.D3_multi_prompt_twin: The it twin (N=50) and the pt-chat repertoire (N=100) ran in multi-prompt batches of B=50 (all five templates of a task; each prompt prefilled at batch 1, KV right-aligned with masked left pads) instead of single-prompt batches, to save GPU time. The CRN uniforms per (task, template, slot) are unchanged, so twin, pt-chat, push, plan-noise and transplant arms stay coupled slot by slot; pushes, plan noise and the transplant arms use single-prompt batches (B=42) with the clean twin as the displacement reference.
deviations.D4_pt_chat_cap: pt-chat cap 640 tokens (exp23's pilot-rule cap) instead of 1,024/1,536: gemma-3-4b-pt under the it chat template rambles (first batch: 10 of 50 rows ran to 1,536 tokens, only 3 closed a fenced code block; 298 s per batch). The first T2 batch (slots 0-9) was generated at 1,536 and truncated to 640 tokens, which is exactly what a 640-capped run produces under CRN sampling (src/truncate_ptchat.py; its labels were recomputed).
deviations.D5_default_rule: D_u needs >= 10 correct twin programs (a logged clarification of protocol v5) and a unique modal label; a tie -> NO_DEFAULT. R6's modal correct label 'linear_scan' (already named by the frozen bench labeller) was promoted to a named extended-catalogue label with a reference that passes 56/56 hidden tests (extensions/R6/linear_scan.py), so R6 is defaulted with D = linear_scan (exp23 had to fall back to binary_search).
deviations.D6_confirmation_batches: Confirmation top-up batches use their natural size (n_passing x 4 rows per template, split at 42) rather than being padded to the fixed shape; coupling is by CRN uniforms, not by batch-mates.
deviations.D7_t2_rule: The T2 re-gate rule (array-based Dijkstra -> 'dijkstra') is a deterministic AST structural check applied in both the runtime and the AST path ahead of the bf_spfa decision (src/regate_rules.py); no new tracer probe was added. It labels the new array-Dijkstra reference, all 219 iteration-4 structural matches and 257 of the 374 iteration-4 'bf_spfa' programs 'dijkstra', and leaves all 10 suite T2 references unchanged (CPU tests T2/T3).
deviations.D8_suite_gold: exp8 suite gold re-check: runtime accuracy 0.804 vs the gate's 0.843 (exactly exp23's D7 value); references 22/22. The suite labeller is used unchanged except for the logged T2 rule.
deviations.D9_holm: Holm across the secondary family (Claim E vs the other secondary claims) is applied by the evaluation step, as planned; raw one-sided p values are reported here.
deviations.D11_massive_set_amendment: COMMIT #1b (before any transplant sample): the plan's literal massive-channel rule (union of per-position top-5 |h| channels over all prompts, band blocks and spec positions) gave 488 channels, most of them position-specific ordinary channels; with it the RND/XT controls would have copied 51-92% of the transplant's own displacement (||d_M||^2/||d||^2 by block). M was amended on activation statistics only to the N_MASSIVE = 5 channels most often in the per-position top-5 (19, 295, 443, 1365, 1698; channel 443 is in every cell's top-5; the five carry 99.1% of ||h||^2). The literal set and its norm report stay in commit_E1.json (predictions/commit_E1b_M.json).
deviations.D12_regate_failure: The style re-gate failed the runtime-vs-adjudicated criterion (bench 0.60, suite 0.50; kappa runtime-vs-AST 0.82 bench, 0.75 suite). All disagreements are pt programs (mostly broken code: runtime 'unknown', both judges 'other'); the 30 it-twin programs agree with the two-family adjudication 30/30. No rule revision addresses broken code, so the pre-declared fallback applies (every runtime/AST disagreement is judged, as the labeller already does), the task below 0.75 on the final label (R1) is flagged, and two sensitivities are added: E-A1 without flagged tasks and beta from correct programs only.
deviations.D13_structural_audit_size: The structural audit reads up to 3 (not 5) programs per (task, model, default/runner-up) group, judged by two families with a tie-break (92 items).
deviations.D14_harness_guard: A pt program that prints a '{...}' line breaks the frozen bench harness's stdout protocol (json.loads on every line starting with '{'); the label worker now records such programs as 'invalid' (labeller_source 'harness_error') instead of failing the whole chunk. Before the guard the worker re-tried one chunk for ~12 minutes (no labels were lost).
deviations.D15_pt_low_correct: Every unit has fewer than 20 correct pooled pt programs (max 18), so beta, r_u and q_base use the pre-declared LOW_CORRECT rule (catalogue labels over all valid attempts, flagged); the pt-chat validity gate failed (0 units with >= 20 correct pt-chat programs) and the primary source is the pooled pt-chat + pt-plain set, as pre-registered.
deviations.D16_split_control_edit: The plan's RND/XT edit (one displacement-targeted vector v = d_M + ||d_ox|| g) failed GPU test U7 at block 11: v is dominated by the massive channels, so bf16-level differences between the live and cached clean states there (|h| ~ 1e4) entered the projection and left the non-massive displacement 13-18% short (cosine 0.998). Before any transplant row was written, RND and XT were re-implemented as a split edit: massive channels move exactly like the transplant (live interpolation to h_pt), the remaining channels get a displacement-targeted move of lam x ||d_ox|| along g (RND: per-sample random unit vector with zero massive components; XT: the donor mean direction). U7 was re-run on the new edit.
deviations.D17_rejudged_disputed: 104 rows left 'disputed' because the inline judge hit HTTP 429 rate limits (85 of them pt plain completions) were re-judged after commit #1 with the same frozen judges; the committed labels and predictors are unchanged and the re-judged labels feed one E-A1 sensitivity (results/rejudge_disputed.json).
deviations.D10_judges: Inline judges on runtime/AST disagreements are the frozen ones (bench j1 gemini-2.5-flash-lite, suite gpt-4.1-mini); the re-gate, structural audit, pt label audit and novelty audit use gemini-2.5-flash + gpt-4.1-mini with deepseek-chat-v3.1 as tie-break.

examples.metadata_code:
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    path = []

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.' and (row, col) not in visited

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col):
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))

        # Explore adjacent cells
        if find_path(row + 1, col) or \
           find_path(row - 1, col) or \
           find_path(row, col + 1) or \
           find_path(row, col - 1):
            return True

        # Backtrack if no path found
        path.pop()
        return False

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
